subject: claurst
title: /sandbox-toggle is a phantom: writes sandbox_mode to ui-settings, no execution path ever consumes it, docs advertise functional isolation
evidence: src-rust/crates/commands/src/sandbox.rs:137 (only writer); sandbox_mode consumers are the command's own status reads at sandbox.rs:44,123 - zero elsewhere in src-rust (grep), no bwrap/sandbox-exec/seatbelt anywhere; docs/commands.md:1183,1253 claim 'isolated environment' and 'Functional on macOS, Linux, WSL2'; TS original had real SandboxManager per spec/02_commands.md:254
one_why: boundary re-review confirms the alleged phantom: port shipped the toggle UI and help text but dropped the enforcement entirely, actively advertising protection that does not exist - the 2-rung misleading tell, and a hard lesson that any copied 'sandbox toggle' pattern must bind at spawn time

subject: claurst
title: project .claurst/settings.json self-grants permission rules - merge guards sibling fields but extends permission_rules from the repo
evidence: src-rust/crates/core/src/lib.rs:2003 (permission_rules extended from project 'over') directly below SECURITY guards carrying base-only for trust_project_mcp_servers/skip_dangerous_mode_permission_prompt/allowed_bash_prefixes at :1992-2001; merged settings feed PermissionManager::new via cli/src/main.rs:496,665-668; evaluate applies persistent Allow rules before mode-default Ask at core/src/lib.rs:2823-2850; also binds headless via ManagedAutoPermissionHandler (core/src/lib.rs:3210-3217)
one_why: a cloned repo shipping one JSON line silences every approval prompt including Bash - the authors demonstrably knew the threat class (adjacent guards + tested MCP-origin forgery fix at core/src/lib.rs:4655-4693) and the guard simply missed this field; our rule loaders must default-deny rules from project scope

subject: claurst
title: project-level hooks merge unguarded and execute via sh -c on tool events; only --bare clears them
evidence: src-rust/crates/core/src/lib.rs:1963 (hooks merge_map override-wins extend over project settings), core/src/lib.rs:3988-3996 (tokio sh -c of entry.command), call sites query/src/lib.rs:1672,1895,1979; clear only under --bare at cli/src/main.rs:530-533; contrast the gated MCP design (core/src/mcp_trust.rs:21-22)
one_why: same trust asymmetry as b2 on the executable surface: opening an untrusted repo yields attacker-chosen shell execution at session/tool events; the repo's own MCP trust model shows the correct pattern (out-of-repo trust store) was simply never extended to hooks

subject: claurst
title: CacheControl type ported but no request builder ever sets a breakpoint - prompt caching absent in practice
evidence: src-rust/crates/api/src/lib.rs:250-262 (CacheControl + ephemeral() constructor); zero call sites of ephemeral()/cache_control outside the api crate (grep across query/tools/cli empty)
one_why: dead port of the upstream caching scaffolding: token-economy credit for 'cache support' is unearned, and cost/latency on long sessions runs full-price; a reminder that porting types is not porting behavior

subject: claurst
title: no provider-level loop tests: ~34k test LOC are unit-level, zero scripted-SSE/faux-provider harness
evidence: grep for mockito/wiremock/httpmock/MockServer across src-rust empty; integration tests limited to 1,366 LOC (core/tests, tui/tests, cli/tests) e.g. core/tests/parity_smoke.rs:22-27,57-60 assert existence-level properties ('contains projects', tokens > 0); CI runs serial cargo test on 3 OS (.github/workflows/ci.yml:22-69)
one_why: the loop, compaction triggers and approval flow are never exercised against a scripted model, so regression risk on exactly the semantics the spec ported is untested - the anchor set's 7-8 verification rungs all have behavior-asserting loop tests; boundary verdict: 20.9k-cited (really ~34k) LOC is partially property-proving, not wholesale
